Unlike the random geometric graph, a pair within the radius is only joined with a probability that falls with distance, so some nodes inside the circle stay unjoined to the central one; the graphs have 2, 7, and 8 edges." width="100%"} Places `n` nodes uniformly at random in the unit cube `[0, 1]^dim` and considers each pair within distance `radius`, as `add_random_geometric_graph()` does. Instead of always joining such a pair, it joins it with probability `p_dist(d)`, where `d` is the distance between the two nodes; by default `p_dist(d) = exp(-d)`. The radius is thus a hard cutoff, and `p_dist` softens the links inside it, e.g. to model a radio signal that fades with distance. Distance is the Minkowski distance of order `p_norm`. The model is due to Penrose; the process follows NetworkX's `soft_random_geometric_graph()`. Each node's position is stored as a list of `dim` coordinates in the `pos_attr=` node attribute. In a directed graph every edge points from the earlier-created node to the later one. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Soft random geometric graphs are useful for: - modeling wireless networks, where links within range still fail with some probability - spatial networks whose link probability decays smoothly with distance - studying how unreliable links change connectivity thresholds ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes. [radius]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Largest distance at which two nodes can be joined. Must be non-negative. [dim]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[2]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of dimensions of the unit cube. Default is `2`. Must be at least `1`. [p_norm]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[2.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Order of the Minkowski distance: `1.0` for Manhattan, `2.0` (default) for Euclidean, or `float("inf")` for Chebyshev. Must be positive. [p_dist]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[Callable[[float], float]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Function giving the probability of joining two nodes at distance `d`. It is called once for each pair within `radius=`. Values of `1` or more always join, values of `0` or less never do. If `None` (default), `exp(-d)` is used. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random number generator. The same `seed=` with the same other arguments always gives the same graph. If `None` (default), the graph differs on every call. [pos_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["pos"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute that stores each node's position. Default is `"pos"`. Pass `None` to skip storing it. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `n=` is negative, `radius=` is negative, `dim=` is less than `1`, or `p_norm=` is not positive. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A hundred nodes, joined within radius `0.2` with probability `exp(-d)`: ::: {#0b47cba7 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_soft_random_geometric_graph(n=100, radius=0.2, seed=6) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (100, 454) ``` ::: ::: With `p_dist=lambda d: 1` every pair within the radius is joined, which is the hard random geometric graph on the same positions. A steeper fall-off keeps fewer links: ::: {#23df227d .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} [ ec.Graph() .add_soft_random_geometric_graph(n=100, radius=0.2, p_dist=p_dist, seed=6) .count_edges() for p_dist in (lambda d: 1, None, lambda d: 1 - 5 * d) ] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [519, 454, 169] ``` ::: :::
